reference.source: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
clinicalPearls: A symmetrical mandibulofacial dysostosis, in contrast to the asymmetry of the oculo-auriculo-vertebral spectrum
Hallmark features are down-slanting palpebral fissures, lower eyelid colobomata with deficient lower lash medial to the defect, and malar (zygomatic) hypoplasia
External ear anomalies with microtia and conductive hearing loss are typical, and audiological support is a priority for language development
Micrognathia and cleft palate contribute to neonatal airway and feeding problems
Intellect is characteristically normal, an important point for family counselling
Most cases follow autosomal dominant inheritance through TCOF1 variants, with variable expressivity even within families
Recessive forms linked to POLR1C and POLR1D and other polymerase-related genes are recognised, so a normal TCOF1 result does not exclude the diagnosis
reference.pathophysiology: The condition results principally from haploinsufficiency of the treacle protein encoded by TCOF1, which participates in ribosomal RNA transcription and processing within the nucleolus. Reduced ribosome biogenesis is thought to trigger nucleolar stress and stabilisation of p53, leading to excessive apoptosis of cranial neural crest cells during early development. Because these neural crest cells populate the first and second branchial arches that form the midface, mandible, and external and middle ear, their depletion produces the symmetrical hypoplasia of the malar bones, mandible, and ear structures. Rarer forms arise from variants in RNA polymerase I and III subunit genes affecting the same pathway.
additionalDifferentials: Nager acrofacial dysostosis (mandibulofacial dysostosis with preaxial limb defects)
Miller syndrome (mandibulofacial dysostosis with postaxial limb defects)
additionalInvestigations: Molecular testing of TCOF1 with reflex analysis of POLR1C and POLR1D when negative
Audiological assessment including bone-conduction and brainstem-evoked response testing
Craniofacial computed tomography to define zygomatic, orbital, and middle-ear anatomy
Sleep study to assess for obstructive sleep apnoea related to airway hypoplasia
Ophthalmological review for eyelid coloboma and ocular surface protection
Genetic counselling and cascade testing of at-risk relatives
redFlags: Neonatal airway obstruction from combined micrognathia, choanal narrowing, and pharyngeal hypoplasia
Feeding failure and poor weight gain requiring nutritional intervention
Exposure keratopathy from lower eyelid colobomata threatening the cornea
Progressive obstructive sleep apnoea with growth or cardiorespiratory consequences
Difficult airway anticipated during any anaesthetic
reference.prognosis: With multidisciplinary craniofacial care, airway and hearing support, and staged reconstruction, most individuals achieve good function and normal cognition, though repeated surgery over childhood and adolescence is often required.
pitfalls: Assuming intellectual disability and thereby underestimating the child's potential
Failing to anticipate a difficult airway before sedation or surgery
Overlooking recessively inherited forms when TCOF1 testing is negative
Neglecting corneal protection in the presence of eyelid colobomata
Delaying hearing rehabilitation, harming speech and language outcomes
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
